clue.text: Spin around and arouse cad after taking stimulants

indicators.note: after puts the cad at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: to arouse someone is to turn them on
taking a drug is being on it
E is ecstasy, so stimulants are Es
a heel is a contemptible man, a cad

explanation.surface: Someone spins round, aroused and acting like a cad once the drugs kick in.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on a drug is 'taking' it; E is ecstasy, so 'stimulants' are Es. 'after' puts the cad last.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on one's heel is to spin round abruptly and walk away, an idiom for a sudden turn.

clue.text: Condiment a little Italian restaurant served up touching lip

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
little means the restaurant word is cut short, losing its tail

parts.note: a trattoria is an Italian restaurant
re, meaning about or concerning, is touching on a topic
lip and sauce both mean cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A small Italian eatery brings out a condiment, served up to go with the lip of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' shortens the restaurant to TRAT, and 'served up', in a down clue, turns ATRAT into TARTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce is a mayonnaise-based dressing served with fish, a classic condiment.

clue.text: Something played live in playing field

indicators.note: in puts the word for live inside the playing field

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British playing field
to live is to be, exist

explanation.surface: Something is played live out on the playing field, like a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The REC (recreation ground) is a public park or playing field in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument, so something one plays.

clue.text: Reveal more attractive clothes come from here

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal their secret
fit is slang for attractive, so fitter is more attractive

explanation.surface: A makeover show: reveal how much more attractive someone is once the clothes come off.
explanation.walkthrough: FIT is British slang for sexually attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or tradesman supplying garments, the source of one's wardrobe.

clue.text: Marine's cocaine supply

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a supple or pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier at sea is caught with a drug supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is read as the adverb from supple, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic is the adjective for the sea, as marine is.

clue.text: Tchaikovsky's First Symphony covers exciting material

indicators.note: covers means the symphony's name goes round the letter

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

indicators.note: First picks the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A concert note says Tchaikovsky's First Symphony includes stirring material.
explanation.walkthrough: The symphony is not Tchaikovsky's but Beethoven's EROICA, wrapped round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually arousing writing or art, material meant to excite.

clue.text: Poet in residence reading or writing?

parts.note: a residence is a home
reading, writing and arithmetic are the three Rs, so either is an R

explanation.surface: A poet in residence asks whether the job is reading or writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the basics of schooling: reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Jolly old soldier, say, catching cab

indicators.note: catching means the outer pieces hold the cab between them

parts.note: ex means former, old
a soldier is one kind of ant, so this is an example
an Uber is a ride-hailing taxi, a cab

explanation.surface: A cheerful veteran hails a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' looks like a military man but is a soldier ant; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of high spirits, much as jolly does.

clue.text: Deny King Edward, say, is making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: a King Edward is a variety of potato, an example of a tuber

explanation.surface: A royal denial: King Edward is staging a return to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to refute or contradict it, to deny it.

clue.text: Very fat figure turns and runs before sumo wrestling

indicators.note: before puts these pieces ahead of the wrestled letters
turns means the number word is turned back to front

parts.note: one is a figure, a number
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: wrestling throws the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A heavyweight turns and runs before the sumo bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means huge, which for a body is very fat.

clue.text: One pound raised during life's works in this list

indicators.note: during puts the raised pieces inside the life story

parts.note: a life, as written, is a biography

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: One pound raised during someone's life ends up listed among their works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns I LB into BLI, and 'during' puts it inside the life story after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibliography is a list of books or writings, so the works are found in it.

clue.text: Sell uniform seen in battle

indicators.note: seen in places the uniform letter within the battle word

parts.note: action is fighting, battle
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Military kit worn in combat is put up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To auction something is to sell it to the highest bidder.

clue.text: National football team containing king's back

indicators.note: containing means the team letters hold the king inside

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, 11, written as two Is

indicators.note: back means the king's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Shakespeare's King Lear, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A national football team picks up a king at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven as figures, 11, looks like II; LEAR'S is turned to SRAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a national of that country.

clue.text: Record about holding vote for a leaver?

indicators.note: holding means the reversed record wraps round the vote
about means the record word is turned round

parts.note: to tape something is to record it
an X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A record of how people voted, perhaps a Brexit ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaver' suggests a Brexit Leave voter but means someone who has left their country; the query flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat lives outside their native country, having left it.

clue.text: Big cheese spread including old wine

indicators.note: including means the spread takes the other letters in

parts.note: pâté is a spread
tent is a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A cheese spread made with vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big cheese' reads as dairy, but means an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a powerful ruler, a big shot.

clue.text: Postal delivery of tea gets protection

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
something in the post is in (the) mail

explanation.surface: Tea arrives by post, packed up for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea that is a postal delivery is CHA IN MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is armour of linked metal rings, worn as protection.

clue.text: Love of the new mobile phone I trouble to bring back

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so the letters shift around
to bring back means the trouble word is read in reverse

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A craving for gadgets: someone with a mobile phone troubles to get it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile phone' reads as one item, but 'mobile' is the anagram signal, turning PHONE into NEOPH; 'to bring back' turns AIL into LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophilia is a fondness for novelty, a passion for anything recent.

clue.text: Post news, a conclusive piece

parts.note: post as a prefix means after
word is news, as in sending word

explanation.surface: A newspaper item: post the news, a decisive story.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterword is a closing section at the end of a book.

clue.text: Work on huge problem for marsupial

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
OS is outsize, a clothing size for huge
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone works on a massive problem involving a marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is an American marsupial, carrying its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Waste long period of time in US prison

parts.note: dung is animal waste

parts.words: long period of time in US
parts.note: eon is the American spelling of aeon, an age

explanation.surface: Wasting years locked up in an American jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell for holding captives.

clue.text: Note on offbeat

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the note after the other piece

parts.note: out means off, as a guess is off or out
do is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician writes a note on the offbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits 'offbeat' into 'off' and 'beat'; the second half is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass them, to beat them.

clue.text: A slice of decent avocado in a little bread

indicators.note: A slice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slice of good avocado inside a small piece of bread, a modest sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in' as part of the definition; it is a link word, and 'a little bread' alone means a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and a centavo is a small coin in several Latin American currencies.

clue.text: Dispense nothing that's beyond Malachi?

parts.note: that's all means there is nothing beyond it
Malachi is a book of the OT, the Old Testament, so it is an example

explanation.surface: Handing out scripture, with nothing past the last prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: Malachi is the final book of the Old Testament, so nothing in the OT comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or allocate, to dispense in portions.

clue.text: Asian drama work not a likely failure

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: not means the letter a is taken out of the work

parts.note: an opera is a musical work

explanation.surface: A review dismisses an Asian stage work as a probable flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone or something with no chance of success.

clue.text: Stroke face of innocent chubby little children

parts.note: a putt is a gentle golf stroke

indicators.note: face of picks the front letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Stroking the innocent faces of plump toddlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are cherubic infant figures in Renaissance art, plump winged babies.

clue.text: Vehicle left key English city

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a key, or cay, is a low island, an isle

explanation.surface: A car left behind in a key English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective, important, but is a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, in north-west England.

clue.text: Parisian's bed? Out of it is out of it

parts.note: lit is French for bed
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A riddling question about a French bed: getting out of it is getting out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of it' is used twice: first as out of bed, then as drunk or high.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit up is slang for drunk or high, which is being out of it.

clue.text: Liking corn mashed up isn't English attitude

indicators.note: mashed up means the letters are crushed and mixed into a new order

parts.note: a mentality is a mindset, an attitude

explanation.surface: A farmer's view: corn crushed up is not the English way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mashed up' rearranges the letters of isn't plus E into SENTI. 'Liking corn' is the definition: corn here means mawkishness, not grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is cheap mawkishness, so a taste for it is sentimentality.
